title: Shi-2024-utility-10.1093/braincomms/fcae165
description: A derivative BIDS-iEEG repackaging of functional-connectivity networks computed from interictal intracranial EEG of 148 epilepsy patients from two centres (HUP and MUSC). Networks cover two re-referencing schemes (common average and bipolar) and 24 connectivity measures across canonical frequency bands, for 2-minute interictal epochs. The dataset supports evaluating how re-referencing and connectivity choices affect the clinical utility of iEEG networks. It contains no time series; the raw recordings are hosted on iEEG.org.
methods_description: Networks were computed with the authors' CNT_Preprocessing_Toolkit pipeline from 2-minute interictal iEEG epochs (up to 5 per patient). Two re-referencing schemes (common average, bipolar) were combined with 24 connectivity measures: Pearson, squared Pearson, cross-correlation, coherence, phase-locking value and relative entropy. The spectral measures were computed in delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma, ripple and broadband ranges. Channel sets were grey/white matter or left/right hemisphere.
